questions.question_text: Under RSA 331-A:16 II, what is the principal broker's primary responsibility regarding salespersons?
distractors: Setting commission rates for MLS
Filing tax returns for agents
Approving all listing prices
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:16, II requires that all licensees and employees associated with a real estate office be reasonably supervised by the principal broker or managing broker. This oversight extends to transactions, trust-account handling (RSA 331-A:13), and advertising (RSA 331-A:16, IV).

questions.question_text: A newly licensed salesperson in NH wants to practice real estate. Under RSA 331-A:2, what must happen first?
distractors: Joining the local REALTOR board
Completing 40 hours post-license
Obtaining personal E&O insurance
questions.explanation: Under RSA 331-A:2, a salesperson must be affiliated with a licensed principal broker before practicing real estate. The broker provides required supervision under RSA 331-A:16 II.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 331-A:16, II, which activity is within the broker's supervisory duties?
distractors: Selecting agents' personal attorneys
Choosing agents' continuing ed
Setting agents' work schedules
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:16, II requires all licensees and employees associated with a real estate office to be reasonably supervised by the principal broker or managing broker, which includes reviewing transaction files and records (see also the 3-year record-retention duties in RSA 331-A:26, XVII-XVIII). Selecting agents' personal attorneys or CE courses and setting work schedules are not supervisory requirements.

questions.question_text: A salesperson leaves one brokerage and joins another. Under Rea 404.02, what must be reported?
questions.correct_answer: The transfer of affiliation to OPLC
distractors: Only the new broker files a formal notice
No reporting is required by either party
The salesperson must file a new license exam
questions.explanation: Under Rea 404.02(c), when a licensee changes affiliation from one principal broker to another, the principal broker must notify the commission in writing within 5 business days, and the change is processed on the commission's Transfer/Activation form, which the receiving principal broker signs to accept supervision. (Former RSA 331-A:17, License Amendments, was repealed in 2023; RSA 331-A:32 concerns civil actions for compensation.)

questions.question_text: A principal broker fails to supervise an agent who mishandles trust funds. Who bears regulatory responsibility?
distractors: Only the individual salesperson is liable
The client who originally deposited funds
The local REALTOR association handles it
questions.explanation: Under RSA 331-A:16, II the principal broker (or managing broker) must reasonably supervise all licensees and employees of the office, and under RSA 331-A:13 and Rea 702.01 the principal broker maintains and is accountable for the trust account. Failure to supervise trust-fund handling subjects the broker to disciplinary action; the salesperson may also face discipline, but supervisory responsibility rests with the principal broker.

questions.question_text: Under Rea 404.04, what must a written listing agreement include?
questions.correct_answer: Fee, expiration date, and parties' names
distractors: Only the listing price and sale amount
Only the seller's full legal signature
Only the detailed property street address
questions.explanation: Rea 404.04(b) requires a listing contract to contain the date of execution; the address, location, description, and asking price; the names and addresses of all parties; the professional fee stated as a dollar amount, percentage, or other consideration; and the date the contract expires. Consent to designated agency or dual-agency showings may also be obtained within the agreement (Rea 404.04(c)-(d)), but an 'agency type' recital is not a required element.

questions.question_text: A buyer wants representation from a NH licensee. Under Rea 404.04, what form of agreement is required?
distractors: A verbal commitment is sufficient
A handshake with the broker
No agreement until offer stage
questions.explanation: Rea 404.04(g) prohibits acting on behalf of a buyer or lessee without a written contract signed by all parties. The contract must state the execution date, a general description, location, and price range of real estate sought, the parties' names and addresses, the professional fee, and its expiration date (Rea 404.04(h)). Verbal or handshake arrangements do not satisfy the rule.

questions.question_text: A listing agreement fails to state the duration of the contract. Under Rea 404.04, what is the status?
distractors: It defaults to a one-year term
It is valid without a duration
OPLC assigns a standard term
questions.explanation: Rea 404.04(b)(5) requires the listing contract to state the date the contract expires. An agreement missing this element does not comply with the rule and should be corrected before proceeding.

questions.question_text: Which element must a buyer agency agreement specify under NH administrative rules?
distractors: The buyer's personal credit score range
The total number of showings allowed
The name of the preferred closing attorney
questions.explanation: Rea 404.04(h) requires a buyer agency/tenant representation contract to state the date of execution, a general description, location, and price range of real estate sought, the names and addresses of the parties, the professional fee, and the date the contract expires. Credit scores, showing counts, and closing-attorney names are not required elements.

questions.question_text: A buyer agency agreement expires during a transaction. What must happen for the agent to continue as buyer's agent?
questions.correct_answer: A new written agreement must be executed
distractors: The agent continues automatically
Verbal renewal is sufficient
OPLC must approve the extension
questions.explanation: Rea 404.04 requires written buyer agency contracts with a stated expiration date, and any extension must be agreed to in writing by all parties (Rea 404.04(k)). Once the agreement has expired with no written extension, no agency relationship exists, so a new written agreement (or written extension signed by all parties) is needed before the licensee can again act as the buyer's agent.

questions.question_text: Rea 703.01's cooperative brokerage agreement rules govern cooperation between a New Hampshire broker and whom?
distractors: All MLS-member brokerages statewide
Other NH brokerages on residential sales
Unlicensed assistants within a firm
questions.explanation: Rea 703.01 allows a licensed NH broker to cooperate with an out-of-state broker on a specific commercial real estate transaction only under a written cooperative brokerage agreement signed before any brokerage activity begins, with the NH broker directly supervising all negotiations, showings, and advertising, and holding any deposits in the NH broker's escrow account.

questions.question_text: A listing broker receives an offer through a brokerage that is not an MLS member. Under NH law, must the listing broker present it?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, all offers must be presented promptly
distractors: No, only MLS member offers are valid
Only if the seller specifically requests it
Only if both brokers are active REALTORS
questions.explanation: RSA 331-A:25-b, I(b)(2) requires a seller's agent to present in a timely manner all offers and agreements to and from the seller, even if the property is already under contract. Nothing in NH law conditions this duty on the offering brokerage's MLS membership or REALTOR affiliation.

questions.question_text: Two brokerages cooperate on a transaction but disagree about the compensation split. What determines the split?
questions.correct_answer: The written agreement between the brokers
distractors: OPLC sets a standard percentage rate
The MLS board determines all split amounts
State law mandates equal commission splits
questions.explanation: Compensation sharing between brokerages is set by contract between the firms — neither OPLC, the MLS, nor state law mandates any split. The listing agreement fixes only what the seller pays the listing firm. Since August 2024, MLSs no longer publish offers of cooperative compensation (a NAR settlement policy change, not an NH statute), so any split must be negotiated and documented directly between the brokers.

questions.question_text: Under Rea 703.01, what must occur before an out-of-state broker works on a NH commercial transaction with a NH broker?
distractors: Payment of a reciprocal licensing fee only
Approval by the local MLS board
Automatic recognition of the other license
questions.explanation: Rea 703.01(a) requires both brokers to agree in writing to all terms of a cooperative brokerage agreement before any brokerage activity begins, on the commission's form. The agreement may not exceed one year, negotiations and advertising stay under the NH broker's direct supervision, deposits go into the NH broker's escrow account, and the out-of-state broker consents to NH jurisdiction (see also RSA 331-A:22-a).

questions.question_text: A listing broker refuses to present a buyer's written offer solely because the buyer's brokerage is not an MLS member. Is this permitted?
questions.correct_answer: No, all offers must still be presented
distractors: Yes, MLS membership can be required first
Yes, non-MLS offers are invalid in NH
Only if OPLC orders the presentation
questions.explanation: While no NH rule forces a brokerage to enter cooperative relationships, RSA 331-A:25-b, I(b)(2) requires a seller's agent to present all offers to the seller in a timely manner — even when the property is already under contract — regardless of the offering brokerage's MLS membership. Withholding the offer would breach that duty.
